item.title: Ladybird Browser Releases First Alpha with Rust Migration and Performance Gains
item.description:
Ladybird Browser Releases First Alpha with Rust Migration and Performance Gains

The Ladybird project has released its first alpha version, allowing users on macOS and Linux to install the browser without the need for manual compilation. This project aims to build a new browser by 2026 with its own implementation of core components including HTML parsing, CSS, layout, and JavaScript.

🔍 Overview

Ladybird is a new browser implementation that builds most of its key components internally while utilizing a few established external libraries for specific tasks.

Component External Library
Text shaping HarfBuzz
2D graphics Skia
Video ffmpeg
Database SQLite

🧩 How it works

The browser architecture focuses on isolation and parallel execution to manage web content efficiently.

  • Process Isolation: Ladybird runs different tabs in different processes, an isolation mechanism used by most modern browsers.
  • Threading: The project has moved style and layout tasks to their own dedicated thread.
  • WebAssembly Engine: The browser replaced its C++ WebAssembly engine with Cranelift, achieving a 7x performance boost on the JetStream 3 WASM benchmark.

⚙️ Key details

Significant technical milestones have been reached through AI-assisted development and rigorous testing:

  • Rust Migration: On February 23, 2026, Andreas Kling reported that parts of the LibJS JavaScript engine were ported from C++ to 25,000 lines of Rust in two weeks using Claude Code and Codex.
  • Web Standards Success: The browser gained 75,650 new passes on the web-platform-tests suite, surpassing Safari. The browser now passes approximately 2.18 million subtests.
  • Rapid Development: Most testing gains occurred between October 22 and October 27, 2026. This followed the release of Claude Opus 5.5 on September 22, 2026, and preceded the release of Claude Fable 5.2 on November 9, 2026.
  • Monthly Gains: The project recorded gains of 30,000 in /css and 10,000 in /editing tests within a single month.

🚀 Availability

Pre-compiled binaries for the first alpha are now available for macOS and Linux.

  • Stability: As an alpha software, the browser may crash or fail to load some websites.
  • Reporting: Users can report broken sites from within the browser and have the option to send crash reports after a failure.
  • Security Testing: The developers are inviting security researchers to hack the browser to help harden the system, noting that no security promises are made during this alpha stage.

#Ladybird #Browser #Rust #WebAssembly #OpenSource

Source: Ladybird’s first alpha release

item.title: Microsoft Launches Edge Lockdown Mode to Disable WebGL and WebGPU
item.description:
Microsoft Launches Edge Lockdown Mode to Disable WebGL and WebGPU

Microsoft has introduced a new Edge Lockdown Mode that disables WebGL, WebGL2, and WebGPU APIs to reduce the browser’s attack surface.

🔍 Overview

  • Edge Lockdown Mode is inspired by Apple’s Lockdown Mode and builds on Edge Enhanced Security Mode (Super Duper Secure Mode), which disables Just‑In‑Time Compilation (JIT) in the V8 engine.
  • It blocks WebGL, WebGL2, and WebGPU APIs to stop privilege‑escapable attacks.

🧩 How it Works

  • The feature focuses on the GPU process, a privileged component that handles complex graphics workloads across browser code, third‑party libraries, and device drivers.
  • When a page attempts to use WebGL or WebGPU, the address bar shows a “Lockdown Enabled” indicator.

⚙️ Key Details

  • Optional, extreme protection for users facing highly targeted attacks.
  • Designed for journalists, executives, security researchers, and administrators (Gareth Evans, Partner Security Group Manager).
  • Accepts reduced website compatibility for stronger defense.
  • Applies to devices in highly restricted environments.
  • Websites that rely on WebGL or WebGPU—especially games or maps—may not work as expected.
  • Users can test the mode in Edge Canary by:
    1. Switching to the Canary release channel.
    2. Enabling the #edge-sdsm-plus flag.
    3. Restarting the browser.
    4. Toggling on Strict mode for “Enhance your security on the web” and blocking WebGL and WebGPU graphics.
  • Microsoft estimates the feature could block around 60 % of privilege‑escalation attacks targeting Edge users.
  • Planned extensions will add more mitigations beyond the GPU process.
  • Experiment results will guide the final experience, adding clearer capability descriptions and site‑level exceptions.

🚀 Availability

  • Currently available only in the Edge Canary channel.
  • Requires a browser restart after enabling the flag.

💡 Why it Matters

  • Provides high‑risk users with an extra layer of defense against targeted cyberattacks.
  • Reduces the attack surface by preventing GPU‑based sandbox escapes.
  • Complements Microsoft’s other security enhancements such as the Edge scareware sensor and the recent restrictions on Internet Explorer mode.

#Edge #LockdownMode #Cybersecurity #BrowserSecurity #WebGL

Source: Microsoft tests new Edge Lockdown Mode that disables GPU APIs

item.title: Chrome adds Gemini‑powered autofill that pulls data from Gmail
item.description:
Chrome adds Gemini‑powered autofill that pulls data from Gmail

Chrome’s enhanced autofill is expanding. Starting today it will use Gemini with Personal Intelligence to suggest information sourced from your Gmail, helping you fill forms without hunting for emails.

🔍 Overview

  • The feature builds on last year’s improvements that added name, passport number, email address, and physical addresses from Google Accounts and services like Google Wallet.
  • It now taps Gmail to surface details such as order numbers, tracking numbers, and travel bookings.

🧩 How it works

  • Gemini with Personal Intelligence scans your Gmail for relevant data when you are completing a form.
  • It can retrieve:
    • Shipment tracking numbers
    • Flight booking numbers or hotel reservations
    • Order numbers of recent purchases
  • The suggestions appear directly in the form fields.

⚙️ Key details

  • All suggested data remains encrypted while displayed.
  • Users can manage what enhanced autofill can access in Chrome’s settings or disable the feature entirely.

🚀 Availability

  • Google is rolling out the improvements today in the United States.
  • The feature is available through Gemini in Chrome for users with Personal Intelligence turned on in the desktop, Android, and iOS versions of the browser.

💡 Why it matters

  • By pulling information from Gmail, the feature can save you the time of searching for confirmation emails, receipts, or shipping updates yourself.

#Chrome #Autofill #Gemini #PersonalIntelligence

Source: Chrome’s enhanced autofill can now pull info from Gmail to help you fill out forms

item.title: Mozilla adds AI form‑filling and webpage‑watching to Firefox Smart Window
item.description:
Mozilla adds AI form‑filling and webpage‑watching to Firefox Smart Window

Mozilla is updating Smart Window — Firefox’s AI‑powered browsing experience — with a new feature that can help you fill out online forms based on your open tabs and watch webpages for changes.

🔍 Overview

  • AI form filling pulls information from the tabs you have open.
  • Webpage monitoring lets you specify pages to watch for sales, job listings, or other updates.

🧩 How it works

  • Click into a form that contains at least four text fields.
  • An option “Fill from sources” appears, showing all open tabs Firefox can draw from.
  • Select or deselect tabs; the browser generates text suggestions based on the content of the chosen pages.
  • The suggestions are generated by Google’s Gemini 3.1 Flash Lite model, with data from your source pages shared with that model.
  • To set up monitoring, type /watch in the Smart Window chat, describe what you’re looking for, and add the webpages you want to watch.
  • Firefox checks the listed pages daily or weekly, but only while the browser is open.
  • When a change is detected, you receive a notification via the Tasks button on the toolbar or a desktop notification (if enabled).
  • Watching pauses after 60 days of no change and stops completely after 90 days.

⚙️ Key details

  • Form‑filling currently supports only text fields; support for dropdown menus and PDFs is under development.
  • Monitoring frequency can be set to daily or weekly.
  • These features are rolling out to the Smart Window beta on desktop in the United States and Canada, with availability in other countries expected in the coming months.

💡 Why it matters

  • Reduces manual data entry by reusing information already open in the browser.
  • Helps users stay informed of updates (sales, job postings, etc.) without constantly revisiting sites.

#Mozilla #Firefox #AIFormFilling #WebMonitoring #SmartWindow

Source: Firefox’s Smart Window adds AI form filling and webpage monitoring
